record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For random Schrödinger operators H = -Δ + V in dimension d=3 with random potential V, are eigenfunctions delocalized in the bulk of the spectrum, do eigenvalues exhibit random-matrix statistics there, and does there exist a mobility edge μ separating Poisson statistics from random-matrix statistics?

evidence.quote: It is believed that in the bulk of the spectrum for d = 3, the eigenfunctions of H are delocalized and the eigenvalues exhibit random matrix statistics. There is also believed to be a so-called mobility edge µ in the spectrum at which the statistics switch from a Poisson distribution to a random matrix distribution. So far this conjecture is wide open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the random Schrödinger operator $H = -\Delta + V$ acting on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^3)$ (or on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$), where $-\Delta$ is the discrete (resp. continuum) Laplacian on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ (resp. $\mathbb{R}^3$) and $V$ is a random potential whose values $\{V(x)\}_x$ are independent identically distributed real random variables (the Anderson model), with disorder strength small enough so that the spectrum contains an interval of absolutely continuous spectrum. Establish the following three conjectures in dimension $d = 3$:

(a) (Delocalization in the bulk.) For energies $E$ in the bulk of the spectrum and for a suitable finite-volume restriction $H_L$ of $H$ to a box of side $L$, the $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions $\psi_E$ of $H_L$ associated with eigenvalues near $E$ are delocalized, in the sense that they are spread out over a region of volume comparable to $L^3$ (e.g., $\|\psi_E\|_\infty \to 0$ as $L \to \infty$).

(b) (Random-matrix statistics.) For energies in the bulk, the local eigenvalue statistics of $H_L$, after rescaling by the local mean level spacing, converge as $L \to \infty$ to the local eigenvalue statistics of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (or, in the appropriate symmetry class, the corresponding Gaussian ensemble).

(c) (Mobility edge.) There exists an energy $\mu$ in the spectrum of $H$, called a mobility edge, such that for energies $E < \mu$ the eigenfunctions are exponentially localized and the local eigenvalue statistics converge to a Poisson point process, while for energies $E > \mu$ the eigenfunctions are delocalized and the local eigenvalue statistics converge to those of the appropriate Gaussian random matrix ensemble.
artifact.status_search_result: The extended-states/delocalization conjecture and the existence of a mobility edge for the 3D Anderson model are well known to be wide open. Localization at high disorder and band edges is established (Fröhlich–Spencer; Aizenman–Molchanov), and Poisson statistics in the localized regime are known (Minami), but no proof of delocalization, GOE statistics, or a mobility edge exists in $d=3$. Recent surveys (e.g. by Spencer, Aizenman–Warzel, Hainzl, and others) continue to list this as a major open problem.

status_evidence.title: Random Operators (Aizenman–Warzel)
status_evidence.snippet: Delocalization and the existence of a mobility edge for the Anderson model in three dimensions remain among the central open problems in the mathematical theory of random Schrödinger operators.
status_evidence.claim: The 3D delocalization and mobility-edge conjectures are open.

status_evidence.title: T. Spencer, Lectures on the Anderson model
status_evidence.snippet: In dimension three, the existence of extended states and a mobility edge is a long-standing open conjecture; only localization at high disorder and at the band edges is rigorously established.
status_evidence.claim: Extended states and mobility edge in $d=3$ remain conjectural.
